title: antennaria howellii subsp. gaspensis
intro: Antennaria howellii subsp. gaspensis, commonly known as Gaspé's rosy-stemmed pussytoes or Newfoundland pussytoes, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the sunflower family that is native to the eastern part of Canada and the northeastern United States. This plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antifungal properties, making it a potential remedy for various ailments such as wounds, skin infections, and respiratory issues. The therapeutic actions of Antennaria howellii subsp. gaspensis include wound healing, antiseptic, and expectorant properties, which can help to soothe and protect the skin, and relieve coughs and congestion. Bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
